20:31.prayer: Father, thank You for giving us this Gospel so that we may believe Jesus is the Christ, Your Son. Nourish the life You give me in His name, and let it grow in me every day. Amen.

21:1.devotion: After the resurrection, Jesus did not vanish from His disciples' lives. John tells us He showed Himself again, this time by the Sea of Tiberias. The risen Lord continues to come near His followers, meeting them in ordinary places and revealing Himself in ways they could see and experience together.
21:1.reflection: Where in your ordinary, everyday setting might Jesus be drawing near to you right now?
21:1.action: Choose one routine place today—kitchen, commute, workplace—and pause there to consciously welcome Jesus' presence.
21:1.prayer: Risen Lord, thank You that You do not leave me alone after seasons of confusion or failure. Open my eyes to notice You in ordinary places today, and help me welcome Your presence with a trusting heart. Amen.

21:2.devotion: John names the disciples gathered by the sea: Peter, Thomas, Nathanael, the sons of Zebedee, and two others. These were men who had followed Jesus, doubted, and believed again. Together they returned to Galilee, and their shared waiting became the setting for another encounter with the risen Christ.
21:2.reflection: Who are the companions walking alongside you in this season of following Jesus?
21:2.action: Reach out to one fellow believer today to pray together or share an encouragement from Scripture.
21:2.prayer: Father, thank You for the gift of companions on the journey of faith. Bless the friends and fellow believers You have placed in my life, and help us encourage one another as we wait for You together. Amen.

21:3.devotion: In uncertainty, Peter announced he was going fishing, and the others joined him. Fishing was his old trade, a familiar path when the future felt unclear. They worked all night and caught nothing. The verse honestly portrays competent effort apart from Christ's direction yielding emptiness.
21:3.reflection: When life feels uncertain, do you retreat to what is familiar instead of seeking Jesus' guidance?
21:3.action: Identify one decision you have been handling on your own, and bring it to God in prayer before acting further.
21:3.prayer: Lord Jesus, when I am unsettled I often grasp for what is familiar. Forgive me for relying on my own efforts alone. Teach me to seek Your direction first, trusting You to lead me where fruitfulness comes from You. Amen.

21:4.devotion: At dawn, Jesus stood on the shore, but the weary disciples did not recognize Him. They had been laboring all night and were focused on their empty nets. John's account gently reminds us that the risen Lord can be near even when our tired eyes fail to perceive Him.
21:4.reflection: What weariness or preoccupation might be blinding you to Jesus' nearness today?
21:4.action: Set aside ten minutes today to sit quietly, asking God to help you notice His presence you may have overlooked.
21:4.prayer: Jesus, You stand on the shore of my struggles even when I fail to recognize You. Clear away my weariness and distraction so I can see You at work. Thank You for coming to me first. Amen.

21:5.devotion: Jesus called out with tender concern: had they caught anything to eat? The disciples admitted they had nothing. His question was not to embarrass them but to draw out their honesty and prepare them for His provision. The Lord begins by naming their need before meeting it.
21:5.reflection: Are you honestly admitting your needs to Jesus, or pretending you have everything under control?
21:5.action: Write down one unmet need you have been hiding, and honestly tell God about it in prayer today.
21:5.prayer: Lord, You ask me honestly about my needs, and You already know them. Help me stop pretending and bring You my emptiness. Thank You that Your care for me begins with Your gentle, searching question. Amen.

21:6.devotion: Jesus directed them to cast their net on the right side of the boat, and the catch was overwhelming—too many fish to haul in. His word turned fruitless labor into abundant provision. The disciples' part was simply to obey His instruction, and obedience opened the way to blessing.
21:6.reflection: Is there a simple instruction from God's Word you have heard but not yet acted upon?
21:6.action: Take one clear biblical instruction you know—forgive, give, encourage, rest—and act on it today in a specific way.
21:6.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your word brings abundance where my efforts bring emptiness. Give me faith to obey even simple directions, trusting that Your instructions are wiser than my strategies. Thank You for meeting obedience with Your generous provision. Amen.

21:7.devotion: When the miraculous catch revealed who stood on the shore, the beloved disciple recognized, "It is the Lord!" Peter's response was immediate and wholehearted—he dressed and plunged into the sea to reach Jesus. Recognition of the Lord stirred eager devotion; he could not wait for the boat.
21:7.reflection: When you recognize the Lord at work, does your heart respond with eager, immediate pursuit?
21:7.action: At the first moment you notice God's goodness today, respond right away with a spoken word of thanks.
21:7.prayer: Lord, give me eyes to recognize You quickly and a heart that responds without hesitation. Like Peter, may I count nothing more urgent than coming to You. Stir fresh eagerness and love in my devotion today. Amen.

21:8.devotion: While Peter swam ahead, the other disciples came in the little boat, dragging the net full of fish to shore. Not everyone responds to Jesus with the same style, but each brought what they had—the catch, the boat, their labor—to the Lord. All reached the same shore where Jesus waited.
21:8.reflection: Are you comparing your way of following Jesus with others' instead of faithfully bringing what you have?
21:8.action: Offer one of your ordinary tasks or resources to Jesus today, doing it deliberately as service to Him.
21:8.prayer: Father, thank You that You receive each of us as we come—some swimming, some rowing, all bringing what we have. Free me from comparison, and help me faithfully bring my work and my days to Jesus. Amen.

21:9.devotion: After a night of fruitless fishing and a miraculous catch at Jesus' word, the disciples come ashore to find a charcoal fire already burning, with fish and bread ready. The risen Lord does not wait to be served; He prepares a meal for weary fishermen, meeting their ordinary hunger with extraordinary care.
21:9.reflection: Where might Jesus already be providing for me before I even ask?
21:9.action: Prepare or share a simple meal today for someone who is tired, busy, or discouraged, without expecting thanks.
21:9.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You meet me in ordinary moments with practical care. Open my eyes to the provision You place before me, and make me willing to offer that same simple kindness to someone else today. Amen.

21:10.devotion: Jesus invites the disciples to add their own catch to the breakfast He has prepared. He welcomes their labor as a real contribution rather than dismissing it. His grace does not make our work meaningless; it gathers what He enables us to bring and sets it on His table.
21:10.reflection: Am I offering Jesus the results of my work, trusting Him to use them?
21:10.action: Present the day's work to God in a brief prayer each morning, asking Him to use your ordinary efforts for His purposes.
21:10.prayer: Father, thank You that my labor is not wasted in Your eyes. Take the small offerings of my hands today, the work I do and the fish I catch, and place them on Your table for Your glory. Amen.

21:11.devotion: Peter drags the net ashore filled with 153 large fish, and the net holds. This vivid detail follows Jesus' earlier instruction about where to cast. The abundance is His gift, and the net that failed to hold nothing now holds everything He provides, pictoring a provision that does not spill or break.
21:11.reflection: Do I trust Jesus to provide what I truly need, even after seasons of empty nets?
21:11.action: Write down one area where you have been striving in your own strength, and pray specifically, surrendering that effort to Jesus today.
21:11.prayer: Lord, I have known nights of empty nets and mornings of unexpected abundance. Teach me to rely on Your word rather than my striving, and to trust that Your provision is sufficient and secure. Amen.

21:12.devotion: Jesus invites the disciples to eat breakfast with Him, and though they hardly dare speak, they know it is the Lord. There is a reverent awe in His presence, yet He welcomes them to a table. Recognition of who Jesus is does not distance them; it draws them to share a meal.
21:12.reflection: Do I come to Jesus with reverent awe, yet trusting His welcome?
21:12.action: Begin a meal today with a deliberate moment of quiet gratitude, consciously acknowledging Jesus' presence before you eat.
21:12.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are holy and risen, yet You invite me to Your table. Give me a heart that recognizes You, that trembles with awe and still draws near with confidence in Your kindness. Amen.

21:13.devotion: Jesus Himself takes the bread and fish and gives them to the disciples. The risen Lord serves His servants, personally distributing the meal. His hands that were pierced now feed His friends, showing that His lordship is expressed in generous, personal care for those He loves.
21:13.reflection: How has Jesus personally served and provided for me, even in small ways?
21:13.action: Serve someone personally today, such as delivering food, pouring coffee, or helping with a task, doing it quietly in Jesus' name.
21:13.prayer: Jesus, thank You that You serve Your people with Your own hands. You have fed and sustained me again and again. Make me a servant like You, glad to give without seeking recognition. Amen.

21:14.devotion: John notes that this is the third time Jesus appeared to His disciples after His resurrection. The risen Christ keeps revealing Himself to His followers, patiently confirming that He is alive. These appearances ground the disciples' faith in real encounters, not vague hope, before He sends them out.
21:14.reflection: Am I building my faith on the risen Jesus, not just on habit or tradition?
21:14.action: Spend ten minutes today reading a Gospel account of the resurrection, asking God to deepen your confidence that Jesus is truly alive.
21:14.prayer: Risen Lord, thank You that You did not leave Your disciples wondering but showed Yourself to them again and again. Strengthen my faith in Your living presence, and let that certainty shape how I live today. Amen.

21:15.devotion: After breakfast, Jesus asks Peter whether he loves Him more than these, likely the boats and the fishing life. Peter, who once denied Jesus, answers honestly without boasting. Jesus responds by entrusting him with caring for His lambs, showing that restored failure becomes the ground for shepherding service.
21:15.reflection: Does my love for Jesus exceed my attachment to my work, comfort, and security?
21:15.action: Identify one attachment competing with your love for Jesus, and take one step today to loosen its hold, such as simplifying or giving.
21:15.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know my love for You, including how incomplete it is. Thank You that You restore those who have failed. Teach me to love You above all else and to care tenderly for Your people. Amen.

21:16.devotion: Jesus asks Peter a second time whether he loves Him, and again entrusts him with shepherding. The repeated question gives Peter space for sincere affirmation, and the repeated commission gives him a renewed calling. Love for Jesus is proven not in words alone but in the steady tending of His flock.
21:16.reflection: Is my love for Jesus showing itself in how I care for His people?
21:16.action: Reach out today to one person in your church or neighborhood who needs encouragement, offering a visit, call, or practical help.
21:16.prayer: Good Shepherd, You ask for love and turn it into service. Give me a heart that cares for Your sheep with patience and humility. Let my love for You be visible in faithful, ordinary care for others. Amen.

21:17.devotion: By the Sea of Galilee, the risen Jesus asks Peter a third time, "Do you love Me?" Peter, grieved yet honest, can only point to Christ's perfect knowledge. Jesus restores this broken disciple not with a lecture about his denial, but with a commission: care for My people. Love for Christ expresses itself in humble, concrete service to others.
21:17.reflection: When failure has left me ashamed, can I still trust Jesus to know my heart better than my guilt does?
21:17.action: Reach out today to someone you may have overlooked or discouraged, offering a simple act of care in Jesus' name.
21:17.prayer: Lord Jesus, You know all things; You know my love is imperfect but real. Heal my failures and turn them into compassion for Your people. Help me serve others today with the humility of someone restored by grace. Amen.

21:18.devotion: Jesus continues His words to Peter at the lakeside. Once Peter was free to go where he pleased, like a young man dressing himself. Now Jesus speaks of a future when Peter's strength will be in another's hands. This is not a threat but honest preparation: following Christ will mean surrendering even his own plans and independence.
21:18.reflection: Am I willing to follow Jesus even when it costs me the independence and comforts I once took for granted?
21:18.action: Identify one plan or preference you are holding tightly, and deliberately surrender it to God in prayer today.
21:18.prayer: Father, I like being in control of my own life. Teach me that belonging to You means trusting You with my future, my strength, and my plans. When following You asks more of me than I expected, give me grace to say yes. Amen.

21:19.devotion: Scripture notes that Jesus' words pointed to how Peter would one day die, glorifying God. Having spoken of that costly future, Jesus gives Peter the simplest and deepest command: "Follow Me." The call stands right beside the cross-shaped cost. Peter's whole life, even its ending, could become an offering of praise to God.
21:19.reflection: What would it look like for my ordinary life today to glorify God rather than serve only myself?
21:19.action: Make one deliberate choice today to follow Jesus in a place where you have recently hesitated or delayed obedience.
21:19.prayer: Lord Jesus, I confess I want the comfort of following without the cost. Yet You call me plainly: Follow Me. Glorify Yourself through my life and even my hardships, and keep my eyes on You rather than on the price. Amen.

21:20.devotion: Immediately after Jesus calls Peter to follow, Peter turns and notices John, the beloved disciple, following behind them. John had been close to Jesus at the supper and had asked who would betray Him. Peter's glance toward his fellow disciple sets up the temptation every believer knows: comparing one's own calling with someone else's.
21:20.reflection: When Jesus calls me forward, do my eyes stay on Him, or do they drift to the people walking beside me?
21:20.action: When you catch yourself comparing your life to another believer's today, pause and quietly refocus on Jesus in prayer.
21:20.prayer: Lord, You have placed specific people and tasks in my path, and different ones in theirs. Forgive my wandering eyes. Keep me faithful to the calling You have given me, and let me celebrate rather than resent how You work in others. Amen.

21:21.devotion: Peter has just been told his own future, and it involves cost. Seeing John nearby, he asks, "Lord, what about this man?" It is a very human question: Will my sacrifice be fair compared to another's? Jesus had said to Peter, Follow Me, and Peter's attention to John shows how quickly comparison follows commitment.
21:21.reflection: In what area of my life am I measuring my obedience against someone else's instead of answering Christ's direct call?
21:21.action: Write down one comparison you have been making with another person, and release it to God in a short written prayer.
21:21.prayer: Lord Jesus, I admit how quickly I ask what about them instead of listening for what You ask of me. Free me from comparison and quiet resentment. Give me a contented heart that loves Your will for my own life. Amen.

21:22.devotion: Jesus gently redirects Peter: whatever the future holds for John is not Peter's concern. Peter's calling is singular and clear: "You follow Me." Christ's plans for each disciple are His own; our task is faithfulness to our particular path. This verse frees us from rivalry and anxiety over God's dealings with others.
21:22.reflection: Can I accept that Jesus' purposes for my life and for others may look different, and still trust Him in both?
21:22.action: Name one person whose path you envy or question, and pray a genuine blessing over them today.
21:22.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your plans for each of Your people are wise and good, even when they differ. Help me stop measuring my life against others' and simply follow You today, trusting Your love and wisdom for us all. Amen.

21:23.devotion: Jesus' words about John spread among the believers and were misunderstood as a promise that John would not die. The Gospel carefully corrects this rumor: Jesus said if He willed John to remain until His return, that was no one else's business. Even faithful communities can distort a leader's words; Scripture models honest clarification.
21:23.reflection: Am I careful to understand and repeat accurately what Jesus actually said, rather than what I wish or assume He said?
21:23.action: Before sharing something you heard today, take a moment to check whether it is accurate, and refrain if you cannot.
21:23.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have passed along assumptions as truth, even about holy things. Give me a love for Your actual words, humility to be corrected, and care for the reputation of others in what I say. Amen.

21:24.devotion: The Gospel closes by naming John as the disciple who testifies to these things and wrote them down, and the community affirms that his testimony is true. This verse anchors the whole Gospel in a real eyewitness and an honest church that stood behind his account. Our faith rests on a trustworthy testimony about Jesus.
21:24.reflection: Do I treat the Gospel's testimony about Jesus as reliable truth I can build my life on, not merely an inspiring story?
21:24.action: Read one Gospel passage carefully today, noting what it actually says about Jesus, and thank God for its trustworthy witness.
21:24.prayer: Lord, thank You for faithful witnesses like John who recorded what they saw and heard, and for the church that affirmed their truthfulness. Strengthen my confidence in this testimony, and make me a truthful witness to what You have done in my life. Amen.

21:25.devotion: John closes his Gospel with a humble admission: the written account of Jesus is only a fraction of all He said and did. Even the world could not contain the books. The Gospel invites us not just to read about Jesus but to keep encountering the living Lord whose work continues beyond any page.
21:25.reflection: Where in my daily life am I still expecting to meet Jesus, or have I closed the story too soon?
21:25.action: Reread one favorite Gospel scene slowly today, then note one way the living Jesus still speaks through it.
21:25.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your story is bigger than any book. Keep my heart open to Your ongoing work in my life and world. Teach me to seek You daily, not only on the pages of Scripture but in every ordinary moment. Amen.
